newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp debt issuance grinds to halt before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp debt issuance grinds to halt before FOMC.

text.p: Corporate debt issuance has come to a grinding halt ahead of Tuesday's meeting of U.S. Federal Reserve policymakers in Washington, dealers said.
"The market's become a virtual graveyard ahead of the FOMC meeting," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Business is on hold until after the meeting."
Although expectations by the market is for no change in monetary policy, players want the meeting out of the way before they proceed with any new business.
The last time the Fed moved was on March 25 when it voted to hike the Federal Funds rate by 25 basis points.

"Most of this week's business is expected to come from the high-yield sector," said another syndicate player. "However, if the tone in the (Treasury) market improves this may spur some investment grade issuers to step in."
Currently, the benchmark 30-year bond is trading off 1/32 at 98-2/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
Meanwhile, $2.2 billion in junk debt is slated to hit the market later in the week, dealers said.
Among this week's batch of new junk offerings is Southern Foods Group $150 million in 10-year 144a senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities.
Price talk on the issue is seen between 325-350 basis points, syndicate sources said.
Golden Ocean Group is slated to bring a $150 million four-year 144a senior subordinated note offering, sources said.
Later in the week, Murrin Murrin Holdings will issue a $400 million two-part debt offering via Natwest Capital Markets, sources said.
The deal is expected to include $300 million in 10-year senior secured fixed-rate notes and $100 million in nine-year senior secured floating-rate notes, sources said.
Another large debt offering will come from Cablevision Systems Corp. The deal is expected to include $300 million 12-year 144a senior debentures via Bear Stearns and Merrill Lynch, sources said.

Among other junk deals expected to come to market are: Bay View Capital's $100 million 10-year note deal via Merrill Lynch, Delta Mills' $150 million 10-year 144a notes via NationsBanc Capital Markets, Giant Industries' $125 million 10-year 144a notes via UBS Securities and Dyersburg Corp's $125 million 10-year 144a notes via Bear Stearns, syndicate sources said.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S. corporate bond unit, 212-859-1675 ))
